spectral.true_color: Dark to medium green vegetation dominates. Pale tan and gray-beige parcels in the northeast and southeast provide the strongest brightness contrast. A smoother green parcel appears along the middle eastern edge. These visible color and texture patterns have high confidence.
spectral.false_color: Vegetated areas appear predominantly red, with bright red patches across the western woodland and eastern green parcel, and darker burgundy patches within the central vegetation. Pale true-color fields become cyan, gray-green or muted pink. Confidence in these displayed patterns is high.

implications.claim: The extensive red response is consistent with substantial live vegetation and relatively strong near-infrared reflectance.
Red intensity differences may reflect canopy cover, leaf area, vegetation type, physiological condition, shadow or display scaling; they do not uniquely measure vigor.
Pale tan surfaces that appear cyan or gray-green in false color likely have low live vegetation cover and may include exposed soil or crop residue.
Darker vegetated patches could include shadow or structural and species differences; elevated moisture cannot be established from their darkness.
Narrow bright lines may be roads or exposed access surfaces, but their material and permeability are unresolved.
No unambiguous open-water body is visible, so water turbidity cannot be assessed.
Small cyan or bright marks are insufficient evidence for buildings because bare soil and mixed pixels can produce similar colors.

spectral.not_revealed: These rendered composites do not provide calibrated reflectances, quantitative vegetation indices, soil or canopy moisture, species identity, crop identity, canopy height, water turbidity, management history or change rates. Image stretching and mixed pixels limit quantitative comparisons. Confidence in these limitations is high.

summaries.w25: High confidence: woodland dominates a rural mosaic with eastern fields. Medium confidence: pale parcels have sparse vegetation. Crop identity, moisture and management remain unresolved.
summaries.w50: High confidence: a connected wooded matrix dominates, with angular fields concentrated in the northeast and southeast. Medium confidence: pale fields contain exposed soil or sparse vegetation, while red false-color areas indicate active vegetation. Narrow access corridors and small openings occur. Crop types, moisture, settlement and recent management remain uncertain.
summaries.w100: High confidence: this 1.2 km patch is predominantly wooded, with agricultural openings concentrated along its eastern side. Medium-confidence visual estimates assign 75% to woody cover, 10% to low vegetation, 13% to pale fields and 2% to linear exposed surfaces. Northeastern fields show parallel bands; southeastern parcels form an angular complex. Strong red false-color responses support extensive live vegetation, but do not quantify health or moisture. Small openings and possible access tracks interrupt the canopy. No unambiguous water body or settlement is resolved. Crop identity, harvest timing, forestry activity and climate remain uncertain.
summaries.w200:
High confidence: the patch contains a connected wooded matrix with managed-looking openings concentrated in the northeast and southeast. Medium-confidence cover estimates are 75% woody vegetation, 10% grass or other low vegetation, 13% exposed or sparsely vegetated fields and 2% narrow exposed corridors.

The northeastern opening has an irregular outline, an east–west dividing line and approximately north–south bands. The southeast contains adjoining angular parcels separated by dark vegetation and narrow lines. A smoother green parcel occupies the middle eastern edge. Small pale openings and diffuse canopy variations occur across the western and central areas; their interpretation as gaps or regeneration has medium confidence.

Extensive red in false color indicates substantial live vegetation with high confidence. Pale tan surfaces appearing cyan or gray-green probably have low vegetation cover, with medium confidence. Red brightness alone cannot establish vigor, and dark tones cannot establish moisture. Roads or tracks are plausible, but buildings and water are not clearly identified. Specific crops, rotation, harvest, irrigation and logging remain unresolved. A temperate or subtropical setting is only a low-confidence possibility.
summaries.w400:
High confidence: this 1.2 km square is a predominantly wooded rural mosaic, with agricultural-looking openings concentrated along the eastern side. Medium-confidence visual estimates assign 75% to woody vegetation, 10% to grass or other low vegetation, 13% to pale fields and 2% to roads, tracks or other narrow exposed surfaces. These estimates are not a pixel classification.

The western and central cells contain a connected, irregularly textured green canopy. Small openings and broad changes in tone interrupt this matrix. A north–south lighter strip near the upper-left/upper-center boundary, a small rectangular pale opening in middle_left and a rounded lighter patch in bottom_center are distinguishable. Their interpretation as canopy gaps, scrub or regeneration has medium confidence.

In top_right, an irregular pale field complex extends roughly 450–500 m across. An approximately east–west line crosses it, and its eastern part contains approximately north–south bands. A smoother green parcel occupies middle_right. The southeastern pale parcel complex spans approximately 450–500 m in each direction within the image and contains angular subdivisions, vegetated separators and access-like lines. Dimensions and corridor interpretations have medium confidence. A narrow corridor follows the eastern edge, while another pale line clips the upper-left boundary.

High-confidence spectral observations include dark to medium green vegetation in true color, widespread red in false color, and pale tan fields becoming cyan or gray-green. These patterns support extensive live vegetation and, with medium confidence, reduced vegetation cover on the pale parcels. Variation in red intensity can arise from canopy structure, vegetation type, shadow and display scaling; it does not independently quantify health or moisture.

Agricultural management is a medium-confidence interpretation supported by parcel geometry and internal bands. Specific crops, rotation, harvest timing and irrigation cannot be established. Forestry, recent clearing and climate assignments have low confidence. No unambiguous water body, settlement, flood pattern or erosion feature is resolved. At native 10 m resolution, small structures, narrow tracks and field edges contain mixed pixels; upsampling does not recover missing detail. A temporal sequence and additional spectral information would be needed to distinguish management stages and environmental processes.
